subject: SLO & benchmark next steps — streaming/latency qualification
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Thompson <sara@latencylabs.io>, Tim O'Riley <tim@latencylabs.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-22T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: SLO & benchmark next steps — streaming/latency qualification

Hi Sara / Tim —

Great to meet today. Quick recap and proposed plan so we have a single source of truth for the qualification work:

Summary of call:
- Latency Labs is validating a low-latency streaming transcription + summary feature for live audio, target 95th percentile latency <= 220ms for per-chunk token responses, with sustained concurrency of ~120 simultaneous streams during peak business hours.
- Key concerns: streaming tail latency, burst concurrency (up to 200 short spikes), and reproducibility of prompt/context handling across model rollouts.
- Security/compliance: customer data stays in their VPC (Dedicated/Private deployment later), but initial benchmark runs can use anonymized audio transcripts sent to Redwood test harness.

Proposed deliverables and owners:
1) Redwood provides:
   - Prompt/response bundle for latency measurement (attached: latency_prompt_bundle_v1.jsonl) — Jasmine
   - Benchmark harness + README with run instructions and container spec (attached: benchmark-harness-readme.md) — Marissa
   - Measurement definitions CSV including metric names, aggregations, and tolerances (attached: measurement-definitions.csv) — Marissa
2) Latency Labs provides:
   - A representative sample of anonymized transcripts (or synthetic audio -> transcripts) for the harness.
   - Target SLO confirmation (95th, 99th targets per route) and preferred concurrency profiles.
3) Schedule: aim to complete a reproducible single-run by 2027-04-30 and a follow-up run with model variant comparisons by 2027-05-07.

Questions / decisions needed from you to proceed:
- Confirm the SLOs you want measured (95th latency, p99, median, and success/error definitions).
- Confirm whether sampling should be deterministic (fixed RNG seed) for the first reproducible runs.
- Are there additional routes or payload sizes we should include (short transcripts / long transcripts / partial context streaming)?

Next steps: I will drop the prompt bundle and harness README in this thread; Marissa will share the measurement-definitions.csv with explicit aggregation windows. Can we schedule a 30m handoff on Mon 2027-04-25 to walk through the harness and mapping of your transcripts to the input format?

Thanks — Jasmine

--
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0143
From: Sara Thompson <sara@latencylabs.io>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Tim O'Riley <tim@latencylabs.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-22T18:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLO & benchmark next steps — streaming/latency qualification

Thanks Jasmine — really helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmed SLOs: 95th percentile token-response latency <= 220ms, p99 <= 400ms for steady-state; acceptable 30s windows for cold-start spikes during model warmup.
- Concurrency profile: baseline 120 steady streams, anticipated bursts to 200 for up to ~90 seconds. We also want a longer-duration 4-hour run to validate stability (memory/kv-cache behavior).
- Deterministic sampling: yes, please make the first runs deterministic (fixed seed). For the variant comparisons we are okay with an additional nondeterministic pass to approximate user-like variance.
- Routes/payloads: deliver 3 buckets — short (<=128 tokens), medium (~512 tokens), long (~2k tokens). Short for live captions, medium/long for detailed summaries.

Security note: we will not share raw audio in this phase; we will transform audio to anonymized transcripts and provide them as newline-delimited items that map to your prompt bundle format. We also asked our security team to review the harness README; they may request a brief security questionnaire about the container image and network egress.

Let's do the handoff on Mon 2027-04-25 09:00 PT — that works for Tim and me.

Sara
Head of Product, Latency Labs
sara@latencylabs.io | +1 (650) 555-0199

Hi Sara, Tim —

Attached are the files Jasmine mentioned. Quick notes on the measurement-definitions.csv and harness assumptions so we avoid ambiguity during runs:

Measurement definitions (high level):
- request_id: unique per transcript chunk
- request_time: wall-clock timestamp at request ingress
- response_time: wall-clock timestamp when first token emitted (streaming) or end-of-response for non-streaming
- token_latency_ms: response_time - token_emit_time for each emitted token; we report median, p95, p99 across tokens per request and aggregated across requests
- success: defined as HTTP 200 + valid structured JSON with \"finalized\": true; any partial stream cut due to connection drop counts as error for availability metrics but still counted in latency distributions where tokens were emitted
- aggregation_window: 60s sliding window for rolling SLOs; 5-minute windows for run-level summaries

Harness assumptions and reproducibility steps:
1) Deterministic seeds: harness sets the RNG seed for token sampling and any synthetic latency injection. Seed is recorded in the run metadata.
2) Model versions: specify exact model artifact sha (we require you to pin model artifacts for reproducibility). Our harness will compare SHA-A vs SHA-B where applicable.
3) Environment: container image (sha), CPU/GPU instance types, driver versions are captured in run metadata; we will produce an environment.json file (attached as part of run bundle) for each run.
4) KV-cache warmup policy: by default the harness performs a 2-minute warmup per model per route to avoid cold-start noise; we can modify based on your request.

Deliverables attached: latency_prompt_bundle_v1.jsonl (prompt+context per line), benchmark-harness-readme.md, measurement-definitions.csv

We'll plan to run an initial deterministic pass on 2027-04-28 (internal execution window) and schedule the joint run with you in the last week of April. Vivek — can you confirm run capacity on Redwood Dedicated for 120 concurrent streaming sessions and whether we can open a 4-hour slot on 2027-04-29?

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Perf Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: SLO & benchmark next steps — streaming/latency qualification

Confirmed — we have a Dedicated slot available and can reserve capacity for:
- 120 steady concurrent streaming sessions + capability to scale to 220 for short bursts (90s) during the run window.
- GPU spec: 8x A100 80GB equivalent for the slot; container images must be provided by Marissa's harness team or use our validated image list.

Reproducibility checklist items from infra side:
- Ensure you pin model artifact sha and provide the harness with the seed (already noted).
- Record network egress rules and drop rates (we will set up a monitoring tap to capture intra-host jitter).
- We will export run-level artifacts (environment.json, run-log.tar.gz, token-level latencies.csv) to the shared Drive link after run completion.

I'll block 4 hours on 2027-04-29 for the stability run; let's keep the 2027-04-25 09:00 PT handoff to confirm mapping and ingestion.

Thanks — Vivek
